name: Rotate MD-11
description: Rotate MD-11F and MD-11P on X-Plane. The flap handle, beacon and HI-INT strobe switches are the aircraft's own, so they are read from Rotate/aircraft/controls/ rather than from the stock datarefs, which this aircraft leaves at zero.
notes: The stock handle dataref reads zero for the whole flight on this aircraft, and the server normalises flaps against the largest value it saw in the flight, so a flight that never reports flaps has no flap position at all: every approach fails the stabilised-approach check with the flaps "at unknown". HubHop has no readable Rotate MD-11 entries; the handle variable is the one the SmartCopilot shared-cockpit configuration for this aircraft synchronises (github.com/radonthetyrant/smartcopilot-rotate-md-11), next to flap_to_sel (the DIAL-A-FLAP thumbwheel) and flap_lim_sel. Its scale is taken to be a 0-1 ratio of handle travel, which is how Rotate's MD-80 publishes its handle (Rotate/md80/systems/flap_handle_drag_position_ratio); that has not been confirmed in the simulator, and if it proves to be degrees or a detent index only the scale step needs changing. On X-Plane every source is a dataref, so a candidate list would always use the first one, and a dataref X-Plane cannot resolve does not fail: it reports nothing, or zero. The handle and the stock dataref are therefore combined with max: whichever one the aircraft actually drives wins, and any other aircraft keeps its stock reading. That is also why the selector can afford to take every X-Plane trijet: the title and ICAO type the Rotate MD-11 reports have not been seen yet, because the flights that showed the fault ran a client that did not read them, and matching on the engine count as well means the profile does not depend on them. Both readings are rounded to a whole percent because the server truncates the value and treats any drop between two samples as the flaps retracting. The beacon and the HI-INT strobes have the same fault: the stock sim/cockpit/electrical/beacon_lights_on and strobe_lights_on stay at zero, so every flight was flagged for running engines with the beacon off and flying with the strobes off. HubHop's Rotate MD-11 entries are only the transponder keypad. The same SmartCopilot configuration lists Rotate/aircraft/controls_c/beacon_lts and strobe_lts among its commands; Rotate names a click controls_c/ and the switch it moves controls/ (controls_c/flap_handle_up and _dn move controls/flap_handle), so the switch positions are read from Rotate/aircraft/controls/beacon_lts and strobe_lts. Those names are inferred from that convention and have not been seen in the simulator. Both switches have a single toggle command where the multi-position landing and nose lights have _up and _dn, so they are taken to be two-position, off at zero; the reading is compared with 0.5 so a switch caught mid-animation counts by the side it is nearer. Each is combined with the stock dataref with or, for the same reason the flaps use max: a dataref X-Plane cannot resolve reads nothing or zero, so a wrong name leaves the stock reading in place, and the other trijets this profile matches keep theirs. If DataRefTool shows different names or a different scale, only these two bindings change.
